title: LightKeeper 2 — a fresh start
summary: LightKeeper was rebuilt from the ground up with a simpler layout, a native window instead of a browser tab, and much faster downloads.
changes: Opens in its own window — no browser needed.
One sidebar with six sections: Aids, Trip, Measure, Water, Weather and Settings. One detail card for everything you click.

The whole USCG Light List (all nine districts, about 54,000 aids) downloads in under a minute on first launch, and every later launch checks for changes in seconds and tells you what moved, changed or was added or removed.
Boat ramps, hotels and parks are properly named. Click one to see its address, phone number and website when they exist.
Right-click anywhere on the map for tides, currents, river gages, dam releases, weather, water temperature, flood alerts, nearby ramps and lodging, or to start measuring.
Hover the map for a subtle hint; turn on 'nearest stations' in the Water panel to see the closest tide, gage and dam stations as you move.
Trip planner: tick aids, set days, speed and hours, and get a day-by-day plan with launch and recovery ramps, lodging, weather, tides and a PDF export.
Measure tool with distance in NM, miles or km and true course per leg. Drag points to move them, right-click to remove.
Water panel: NOAA tide and current predictions, USGS river gages (level, flow, temperature), USACE dam pool, inflow and outflow.
Backup sources: if the National Weather Service or NOAA tides are down, forecasts and tides come from Open-Meteo so you still get data.

Works offline: the Light List, places, station lists and every map tile you have viewed are cached in your AppData folder. After first launch the app also pre-caches the US base map, satellite imagery around every aid, and ramps and lodging per district in the background.
NOAA ENC chart overlay (Charts button) with caching.
District picker filters the map to one district or shows all.
Zoom all the way to street level on every base map.
Settings: vessel speed and fuel, offline map downloads, backup export/import of your settings and saved trips, optional Mapbox key.
Fixed: secure connections to map and chart services on PCs whose Windows certificate store is out of date.
